summary: Discovery focused on integration options for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer uses LangChain/LlamaIndex in pipeline, needs VPC/private control for PHI-adjacent workloads, asks about SDKs, gateway/proxy, rate limits, observability hooks and benchmarking. Agreed next steps: pricing, SOC2/network docs, sample prompts for perf benchmark, schedule deep-dive.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of AI, Emerald), Sam (Platform), Lena (Security), Tom (intern)

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE, with me is Diego our solutions engineer. quick confirm i'm seeing priya, sam and lena?
00:12 - Priya: yep hi hi, thanks for making time.
00:16 - Diego: great, i'll try to keep it technical and focused on integrations — we can cover SDKs, langchain support, gateway ideas, quotas, that sort of thing.
00:28 - Sam: perfect, our main goal today is to understand how Redwood would sit in our infra for both hosted and potentially private deployments. we run a mix of PHI-adjacent workloads so security is big for us.
00:39 - Maya: totally, noted. quick context from our side: Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem options. we also have SDKs in python/js, and connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex, plus observability hooks.
00:55 - Priya: you said connectors — is that a first-party connector or examples? we've built a bunch of glue code for Lang Chain so curious how plug-and-play it is.
01:07 - Diego: we have first-party SDKs and a set of examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex; most customers either use our SDK directly or use the LangChain wrapper — sometimes slight adapter work depending on streaming and function-calling. oh and sorry i said langchain as two words earlier —
01:20 - Priya: (laughs) yeah. we need streaming for some real-time summarization.
01:24 - Diego: streaming supported on hosted and dedicated, on private it depends on network setup but yes we support chunked streams and callback hooks.
01:33 - Sam: our infra constraint: everything must go through our egress gateway/proxy, we have strict mTLS and header-based auth. can your client support proxying and custom header insertion?
01:45 - Diego: yes — SDK supports http proxy config, and we can accept forwarded headers. for Dedicated and Private you can also route via our gateway or run a local gateway in your VPC that proxies to the Redwood control plane.
01:57 - Lena: + security note: we require KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for model requests. does Redwood provide per-request audit logs and do you support our KMS?
02:09 - Maya: short answer: yes. we have audit logs (request-level metadata) in the console and an API ingest for logs. for KMS we support customer-managed keys via common cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM integrations for Private deployments.
02:25 - Lena: ok good, and encryption at rest for cached KV? we do prefix caching of embeddings so that matters.
02:33 - Diego: our KV cache can be disabled or configured to use customer-managed encryption in Private; in Hosted it's encrypted at rest — we can provide specifics in the security pack.
02:42 - Priya: about costs — we run many short generation calls and some longer chat sessions. what's the trade-off engineers see between hosted and dedicated re: latency and per-token cost?
02:55 - Maya: good question. hosted is easiest to get started but unit cost is generally higher. Dedicated gives lower per-token cost and more predictable throughput (also SLO). Private is for data residency and strict network control — latency depends on your infra placement. Diego, want to add?
03:08 - Diego: yes, performance wise Dedicated lets you control GPU shape and batching — for lots of small requests we can tune batching and caching to reduce token cost while keeping latency under your SLO. typical tuning: concurrency, batch window, and prefix caching. sometimes customers build gateway-level multiplexing to further amortize overhead.
03:28 - Sam: we use LangChain + LlamaIndex for retrieval augmented workflows; the index hits embeddings store and then we call generation. curious about embeddings pipeline — do you support separate rate limits and quotas for embeddings vs generation?
03:43 - Maya: yes, rate limits are per-route/model — embeddings are metered separately in our billing and quota system; you can set token quotas per API key and per-organization.
03:54 - Sam: what about per-route QoS, like reserve throughput for critical endpoints and throttle experimental ones?
04:01 - Diego: we have routing policies — you can pin a model to a route, set priority, and have fallback policies. for Dedicated you can reserve pools for critical routes, and we support canary routing.
04:12 - Priya: ok, can we plug in observability? we need distributed tracing tied to our request IDs and token-level cost breakdowns.
04:21 - Diego: we emit tracing hooks — you can forward X-Request-Id and we keep it in logs; console shows token-level cost and latency per-request. we can also stream traces to your datadog/newrelic via webhook or log export.
04:36 - Lena: is there an SDK hook to inject our internal trace context (w3c traceparent)? sometimes the auto-instrumentation drops context.
04:44 - Diego: yes, our SDK accepts custom headers for tracing and we propagate them. small caveat: if you're using the LangChain wrapper you may need to plumb headers through the adapter — we have examples.
04:58 - Priya: sweet. about model variants — we sometimes want a cheaper quantized model for background tasks and a higher quality one for customer-facing flows. support for automatic fallback?
05:10 - Maya: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible variant if capacity or pricing policy triggers it. you can define policies per-route. Diego can share the policy config example.
05:20 - Diego: i'll do that. also on quantization: Dedicated supports popular quantized runtimes and we've got profiles that trade quality vs cost.
05:27 - Sam: our biggest gotcha has been latency spikes due to cold KV caches and long tail latencies. do you do prefix/KV caching and warm pools?
05:38 - Diego: yes we do prefix caching and keep-warm strategies — with Dedicated you can set a minimum pool size and elastic burst. Hosted has warm pools but dedicated gives more control.
05:49 - Priya: integration specifics — we use LangChain chains with callbacks for streaming tokens to client. is there a direct callbacks integration or do we need to rewire?
05:59 - Diego: our SDK supports async streaming callbacks; LangChain examples show how to wire callbacks into the chain handler. occasionally Llama Index examples require a small shim but we've done this for a number of customers.
06:12 - Tom: (intern): will there be a dev sandbox we can use to test?
06:15 - Maya: yes, we provide sandbox keys and credits for POC.
06:19 - Priya: for compliance, we need SOC2, ISO docs and a network diagram for Private plan. can you share that?
06:28 - Maya: absolutely — we'll attach our SOC2 report and a reference network diagram; for Private we'll provide a customer-specific diagram.
06:36 - Lena: also SSO integration — we need SCIM + SAML to provision accounts and RBAC controls.
06:42 - Diego: SCIM and SAML SSO are supported; RBAC with custom roles is available in our console.
06:47 - Priya: timelines — we want to pilot within 6 weeks if possible. is that realistic?
06:53 - Maya: yes, for a hosted POC it's quick — Dedicated pilot depends on capacity sizing but 4-8 weeks is typical. Private/on-prem takes longer for network and security review.
07:05 - Sam: any requirements for gateway certs? we do mTLS egress.
07:09 - Diego: we support mTLS — for Private you can also terminate inside your VPC.
07:14 - Priya: ok, let's talk about benchmarking — we'll give you a set of 50 representative prompts and traffic shape, can you run a performance run and show token-cost tradeoffs across a hosted vs dedicated config?
07:25 - Maya: yes that's what we normally do; Diego will lead that and we'll provide a spreadsheet with expected throughput, median/95th latency, and cost estimates.
07:35 - Diego: one minor note on perf: if your prompts do a lot of context retrieval (long context windows), kernel selection and runtime compile choices matter. we'll pick a model profile that matches your seq length distribution. sometimes names get fuzzy in transcripts — redwood runtime, r redwood ded...sorry — but the point is we tune kernels and quantization.
07:56 - Priya: haha that's fine. question on SDK language support — we primarily use python, but some services call from node microservices. do you have both?
08:05 - Maya: yes python and node SDKs and a simple curl API. we also have community examples for Java and go.
08:12 - Sam: regarding quotas: can we set per-team API keys with separate quotas and alerting when nearing limits?
08:18 - Diego: yes per-key quotas, alerting hooks, and per-route throttles. we also support usage tiers to throttle non-critical teams.
08:27 - Priya: how granular are logs? we need to link requests to our internal user ids but we cannot log PHI content. can you redact payloads and still keep metadata?
08:37 - Diego: yes, you can configure request payload redaction and keep metadata like token counts and response latencies; we also offer replay tokens for debugging in a controlled way in Private.
08:48 - Lena: replay tokens — are those auditable? we need to ensure access control to replays.
08:53 - Maya: yes access governed by RBAC and audit logs. we'll include details in the security pack.
08:59 - Priya: any enterprise pricing models for committed Dedicated pools?
09:03 - Maya: yes reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits and discounts — we'll send tiers and example Sizing for your expected throughput.
09:11 - Sam: for the gateway idea: we have an internal proxy that does batching and request coalescing. we'd prefer to keep that so Redwood needs to accept batched requests equivalently.
09:23 - Diego: supported — we can accept batched payloads (we'll need to discuss alignment on header propagation and trace ids).
09:30 - Priya: do you support function-calling / structured outputs? we use that heavily for extracting structured fields.
09:36 - Diego: yes function/tool calling and structured JSON output supported; we also have schema enforcement tools to reduce hallucination for critical fields.
09:45 - Priya: great. any gotchas for LlamaIndex integration? we had one issue with streaming and the index iterator.
09:52 - Diego: sometimes the Llama Index loader needs a shim for streaming; we have sample shims and a repo with examples.
10:00 - Maya: quick recap of open concerns: security docs + network diagram, pricing and Dedicated sizing, sample prompts for benchmark, SDK examples for LangChain/LlamaIndex, and scheduling deep-dive. agree?
10:12 - Priya: yes agreed.
10:15 - Lena: one follow up: can we get a short note on retention policy for logs and how deletion workflows work?
10:20 - Maya: yes will include retention and deletion SLA in the pack.
10:24 - Sam: any limitations on tokens per request for streaming?
10:28 - Diego: max token limits vary by model — we'll include the specifics per model profile in the benchmark doc.
10:33 - Priya: last question — if we do a hybrid where some workloads go Dedicated and others hit Hosted, how do you handle routing?
10:40 - Diego: policy-based routing: you can route by route key, headers, or model; we support region-aware and cost-aware routing and automatic fallback to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
10:52 - Priya: awesome. ok thanks everyone.
10:55 - Maya: thanks — we'll send the pack and proposed benchmark spreadsheet. Diego will reach out to schedule the technical deep dive.
10:63 - (sic) Sam: typo in timestamp but you got it.
11:00 - End of recording.

Notes: transcript includes minor mis-attributions and occasional transcription artifacts; timestamps approximate.
